findings.observation: Local known_clean/error state; active and operating are committed once under the outer catch gate. A later entry cannot be poisoned by a previous catch.
Public owned/failure access avoids operation-owned mutable fields while operating is true. Thread/fiber and active/poison gates stay mutex-protected.

Existing PTD is borrowed and left installed. Fresh initial-locale PTD is owned through checked detach, one destructor, observed raw final free and checked slot clear; errno/doserrno8bytes only may differ from snapshot.
Known detach failure leaves published root; known root free failure retains destroyed root and sentinel; clear-only retry does not repeat destructor/free. owned is false after known root release.
Allocation/publication/constructor/free or unsupported PTD mutation retains active poisoned state and provider lease. Native leave cannot return API success on failed cleanup.

Final core children terminate only after active-and-poisoned predicates via own-process TerminateProcess151..155; generic SIGABRT239 cannot satisfy them. Native cleanup abort observer requires raw-denied marker for163; callback return230 fails. Earlier ambiguous exit attribution is corrected.

ProviderLease retains stable binding index/heap/locale/locks; foreign paths do not read DomainStorage controller phase/busy. Thread plus fiber identity is checked and bookkeeping preserves incoming/outgoing LastError.

Single active body across sequential host threads. Gate is released during PTD/native/provider/wait calls. Warming/control/overlap/reentry/stopped entries reject before body; active permission survives pause until PTD leave.

limits: PTD raw allocation deliberately bypasses recovered calloc/new-handler/errno fallback; this is a selected source ownership bridge, not original CRT/EH equality
Only initial locale and errno/doserrno mutation are supported for new scope-owned PTD; dynamic locale/other PTD changes poison
Worker and callback shared fallback/OOM/state/stream concurrency remains an explicit ready-proof contract; synthetic integration finishes own fake workers before foreign publication
General overlapping callback success, callback reentry, actual foreign game thread behavior and runtime hooks are not established
Thread/fiber identity checks are source-reviewed; tests use own std::threads and do not switch actual fibers
External admission stop and cleanup must exclude newly generated native callbacks; provider stop is not disabled-hooks or image-unload proof
Existing native raw/unknown failures are retained conservatively; no invented rollback or safe-unload claim
